validation.notes: Root cause: packages/coding-agent/src/migrations.ts migrateSessionsFromAgentRoot() computed the target directory with cwd.replace(/^[/\\]/, '').replace(/[/:]/g, '-'), so Windows backslashes were never converted to '-' (drive-letter cwds additionally kept their colon, e.g. 'C:\Users\dev\work\app' -> '--C:-\Users\dev\work\app--' instead of '--C--Users-dev-work-app--', and UNC '\\fileserver\team\app' -> '--\fileserver\team\app--'). Legacy session files were therefore moved into directories the session manager (core/session-manager.ts getDefaultSessionDirPath, which already uses /[/\\:]/g) never reads. Fix: one-character change adding the backslash to the replacement character class, restoring the documented encoding (drop exactly one leading '/' or '\', then map every '/', '\' and ':' to '-'). No other production code changed. Regression: .prale-eval/regression.mjs loads the real TS module through .prale-eval/subject.mjs loadModule, faking only the agent/config-dir boundary (getAgentDir/getBinDir/CONFIG_DIR_NAME/chalk/keybindings/stripBom) and using a real scratch filesystem under .prale-eval/.tmp-regression (removed in a finally block) so byte preservation and rename semantics are genuine. It asserts: drive-letter backslash, drive-letter forward-slash, UNC and POSIX cwds each land in the exact expected 'sessions/--<encoded>--' directory; no session directory name retains ':' or '\'; moved session bytes are identical to the originals (multi-byte UTF-8/CRLF payload); invalid headers (wrong type, missing cwd, malformed JSON, blank first line) and non-.jsonl files are left untouched and create no directory; an existing destination file is never overwritten and its source is left in place; a second migration run is idempotent and does not throw. Two-state validation performed: with the fix the script exits 0; after temporarily reverting the regex to /[/:]/g it exits 1 with AssertionError 'cwd "C:\\Users\\dev\\work\\app" must migrate into --C--Users-dev-work-app-- ...', then the fix was restored (git diff shows only that one line). Node 24.14.0 provides TypeScript stripping and VM modules, so no dependencies or network were needed; the only output noise is Node's ExperimentalWarning for stripTypeScriptTypes/VM Modules.
